sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-08-v16-full/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 33 (#32 criteria_are_outcome_based_and_browser_decidable) and Internal Quality Checks row 33 (no annotation on #32; row 34 #33 carries the Mukesh flow-bundling note)
v15 hosted run reward-details.json for kTaeUNx (Oracle) and RUAQ5Z4 (GPT-5.6-luna) judge reasonings for the restore, live-library, isolation, dynamic-code and stale-save criteria
evidence: Checked all 55 criteria (render 1, constraints 2, functional 43, polish 6, visual 3). Every binary criterion names a concrete action and a browser-observable end state with explicit fail conditions. Durable evidence is used where state matters: cw_shared_saved_record (constraints/judge.toml:27) and cw_save_reload_restart (functional:339-345) clear origin storage, reload and use the restart_app tool. cw_restore_request_repeat_safe (functional:375-381) passes or fails on the revision count in a freshly loaded page, not on the reply status. Negative claims have positive controls and judge-chosen distinctive probes. Examples: payload markers built from two halves in cw_dynamic_code_refused (functional:330-336); in cw_preview_isolation (functional:321-327) a silent probe counts as not performed; cw_newer_revision_notice_keeps_draft (functional:402-408) has a 10 s no-notice baseline; cw_stop_cancels_pending_work and cw_newer_run_supersedes (functional:303-318) wait 8 s with void-attempt rules. No criterion relies on reading source, a response shape alone or a probe that leaves no trace. cw_custom_document_surface (constraints:18) decides from live-DOM facts only, and its prompt forbids file names and bundle names. No criterion tries to grade SQLite or another fact the browser cannot observe. The brief makes restores ordinary HTTP requests (behaviour.md, last paragraph), so recording and replaying one is a public, observable route. The v15 Oracle and GPT judge reasonings show request bodies were visible and replayable ("POST /api/snippets/6/restore ... body {revision:2, sourceRevision:1, operationId}"; "historyId ... requestId"). Broken-app trial: in v15 the GPT app over-passed cw_live_library_update by an existing snippet's rev bump and cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state without scroll and Undo checks. The v16 wording now requires a new unique title, then a rename, unchanged scroll and Undo back to the pre-marker draft, so those shortcuts fail. Conforming-alternative trial: a WebSocket-only restore would fail the replay, but the brief requires HTTP restores. An optimistic-concurrency replay that returns 409 still passes because only the revision count is graded. Note, not a defect: the three visual criteria (visual/judge.toml:18,34,50) are craft likert with an anchor at every level and a fixed observation procedure (1440x900, Run, caret screenshot, double-click selection). That is the shipped likert format the skill names as a known false positive, and row 41 governs it. Minor: cw_custom_typing_and_line_join's clause "text can only be changed by setting it programmatically" is not directly observable, but it reduces to the real-key typing steps already listed. Risk=true because there is no configured-judge run on these v16 bytes. The index states hosted runs exist only for v15, whose functional criteria differ, and scripted Playwright golden runs are not LLM-judge decidability evidence. So no measurement yet shows the revised timing-sensitive (Stop/supersede code-runner) and multi-step (restart+replay) criteria are decided reliably by the configured judge. The v15 audit noted 4 over-passed criteria.
